text:
Vitali Pinchuk took the long road to Nashville. Never drafted, he spent six seasons with Dinamo Minsk in the KHL and broke out last season with 66 points in 65 games, roughly 60 points over 82 NHL games by our league translation. The Predators signed him in April, and he played his first NHL game on Oct. 10.

His first NHL goal came on Nov. 5 against Colorado, in an overtime win that Sports Illustrated headlined "First NHL Goal, First NHL Blood, Vitali Pinchuk Drives Predators to Victory." Nashville has not lost since.

The numbers worth watching are his chances. In about nine minutes a night he has 1.91 expected goals on his own shots (1.27 per 60 minutes), a strong rate for a depth forward, against one goal. His shot is not overpowering by NHL tracking, so he is getting to good spots. With only ten games, our season range is wide: 12 to 30 points. If his minutes grow, he is the kind of player whose goals catch up to his chances.
headline: Pinchuk is getting chances in small minutes
